SMTO-TSK-0050 — A value given to this workflow isn't accepted

GUID: 963ef3d1-35f4-4abb-be59-5ceb7344fd79
Slug: recipe-parameter-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This workflow takes some input values, and at least one was missing, unexpected, or the wrong kind (for example text where a number is needed). SMTO didn't start the workflow.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check where the inputs came from: if a schedule started this workflow, open Schedules and check that schedule; if you started it, check the values you gave. The wrong value comes from whatever started the workflow, so that is where to correct it.
  2. Give each input the kind of value it expects, such as a number for a count or plain text for a name, and leave out any input the workflow doesn't use. SMTO only starts a workflow when every input is present and of the right kind.
  3. If this is a learned workflow, open the conversation where it was taught and open the details of one of its tool steps and select Teach workflow from this run again to save a fresh copy. A fresh copy stores input rules that match the steps it runs.

What success looks like

  • The workflow starts and opens a conversation showing its progress.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the workflow, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep starting it with the same values; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recipe parameter validation rejected the supplied or saved values: a value is unknown, missing or of the wrong type, a declared name is duplicate or invalid, a constraint is unsupported, a number is not finite, a step binds an undeclared parameter, or the values exceed 64 KiB.

What this means

  • Recipe parameter validation finds unknown/missing/wrong-typed values, duplicate/invalid names, unsupported constraints, non-finite numbers, undeclared bindings or excessive total parameter size. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Recipe parameter validation finds unknown/missing/wrong-typed values, duplicate/invalid names, unsupported constraints, non-finite numbers, undeclared bindings or excessive total parameter size.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe parameter names/types/constraints and the 64 KiB aggregate bound without exposing private values.

How to fix it

  • Compare the supplied agent_recipe_parameter_values (and the recipe's default_parameters) with the recipe's parameter_schema: supply every required name with its declared type (string, number, boolean or json), remove undeclared names, keep validation to enum/minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength/format, and keep the encoded values under 64 KiB. Correct the inputs before running again.
  • Use the current recipe parameter schema and supply each required value with its declared type.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Required values and declarations pass the current recipe's complete parameter contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
